title: Filtering the sales table by numbers · part 18

steps.title: Keep customer_id >= 9
steps.prompt:
Numbers compare with small symbols:
  > bigger   < smaller   = exactly   != not equal
Keep the rows where customer_id is at least 9.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM sales WHERE customer_id >= 9;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM sales.
Add WHERE after the table name.
The test is customer_id >= 9.
Write: SELECT id FROM sales WHERE customer_id >= 9;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM sales WHERE customer_id >= 9;
steps.memory_trick: WHERE keeps only the rows that pass the test.

steps.title: Count rows customer_id >= 9
steps.prompt: COUNT(*) counts how many rows survive the filter.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT count(*) FROM sales WHERE customer_id >= 9;
hints: Start with SELECT count(*).
FROM sales.
Add WHERE customer_id >= 9.
Write: SELECT count(*) FROM sales WHERE customer_id >= 9;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM sales WHERE customer_id >= 9;
steps.memory_trick: count(*) + WHERE = 'how many pass?'

steps.title: Filter then sort: customer_id >= 9
steps.prompt:
Filter first, then ORDER BY tidies what is left.
LIMIT 3 keeps the top of that sorted list.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM sales WHERE customer_id >= 9 ORDER BY customer_id LIMIT 3;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM sales.
Add WHERE customer_id >= 9.
Add ORDER BY customer_id LIMIT 3.
Write: SELECT id FROM sales WHERE customer_id >= 9 ORDER BY customer_id LIMIT 3;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM sales WHERE customer_id >= 9 ORDER BY customer_id LIMIT 3;
steps.memory_trick: WHERE trims, ORDER BY sorts, LIMIT cuts.
